html:
SMTO-CMP-0036 — A step that should have made a change didn't report success

GUID: c6745dca-d64a-4699-a951-4a9495c45b49
Slug: completion-neutral-write-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI pointed to a step that was meant to change something. That step ran to the end but didn't report success, so it doesn't show the change worked. SMTO asked the AI to check the result.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to check whether the change took effect. Looking at the result is the only way to know, since the step itself didn't say.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, expand the task and open that step to read its output and any error text. The output often explains why the step didn't report success.
  3. Check the thing that was supposed to change, or send a message asking SMTO to check it without changing anything. The change may have happened anyway, so repeating it could apply it twice.
  4. If the check shows the change is missing, ask SMTO to fix the cause shown in the step's output and try again. Fixing the cause first keeps the same problem from happening on the next try.

What success looks like

  • A check shows the change is in place and the task finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them, with the step's output, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the change until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because a cited write operation has neutral status completed (the process exited with a nonzero code) rather than success; a neutral write receipt does not establish semantic success.

What this means

  • Cited evidence is a write classified completed rather than success and cannot qualify as a complete read observation. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Cited evidence is a write classified completed rather than success and cannot qualify as a complete read observation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original write receipt and authoritative post-state rather than promoting neutral completion to semantic success.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the cited write receipt (exit_code, stderr) and the actual post-state of the target resource. Cite a successful effect receipt or a fresh read observation of the post-state; a neutral process exit is never promoted to success, and the write must not be replayed while its effect is unconfirmed.
  • Verify the mutation post-state; a neutral process exit alone does not prove semantic success.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended change is established by eligible success/post-state evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
